projects.title: Project Mordred
projects.short: A private assistant, shaped around my needs.
projects.summary: A private personal AI assistant with a tunable personality, with tools and features added one by one as my needs develop.
projects.motivation: I wanted a private personal assistant whose personality I could tune to my liking. Mordred is an ongoing project where I integrate tools and features one by one, following what I need from an assistant.
projects.contribution: I define the assistant’s personality and desired behaviour, develop the feature ideas, and design workflows such as conversational reminders.
projects.approach: Mordred uses Telegram for conversation, local model serving through LM Studio, and PostgreSQL for reminder storage. The reminder workflow detects intent and extracts a title, date, and time. The backend runs on my homelab.
projects.outcome: Saving and deleting reminders worked in a few manual cases. Scheduled notifications and longer-term behaviour still need testing. Web search and retrieval-augmented generation are future plans.
projects.reflection: I’m learning how to turn the behaviour I want from an assistant into connected features and workflows.
projects.cardOutcome: Reminder creation and deletion tried; scheduled notifications still need testing.

projects.title: Glucode
projects.short: Read the label. Keep the food card.
projects.role: Product concept · user flows · Figma prototype
projects.summary: A nutrition-label scanner and summarizer with reusable food cards and daily intake tracking.
projects.motivation: Nutrition labels provide useful information, but reading and interpreting them takes effort. People may overlook how individual snacks and drinks contribute to their daily intake, especially when checking every label feels inconvenient. Glucode was designed to reduce that effort.
projects.contribution: I originated the concept, defined the features and workflow, and created the Figma prototype that informed the application. This was a four-person project across Applied NLP, Applied Computer Vision, and HCI.
projects.approach: The application scans nutrition tables, summarizes the information, and lets users save reusable food cards. Logging a saved card adds its nutrition to daily intake without scanning the same product again. My original proposal used the Gemini API; final backend and model implementation were handled by teammates.
projects.outcome: The team completed and demonstrated the application in class. The project included versions for the NLP/CV and HCI coursework.
projects.reflection: My strongest contribution was connecting the initial problem to a clear set of features and user flows.
projects.cardOutcome: Team application completed and demonstrated in class.

projects.title: Credit Risk Predictor
projects.short: From a dataset to a prediction app.
projects.summary: An individual MLOps assignment covering preprocessing, classification-model comparison, a prediction application, and Docker packaging.
projects.motivation: Explore the workflow from tabular borrower data to a usable credit-risk prediction application.
projects.contribution: I designed the workflow, ran notebooks, reviewed results, published the application, and built and ran its Docker container.
projects.approach: The coursework used 32,581 records with 11 input features and compared Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost. The workflow included missing-value handling, numerical scaling, categorical encoding, and saved model artifacts for the application.
projects.outcome: The report documents a hosted prediction app and a successful local Docker build/run. These are coursework results, rather than evidence of use in lending decisions.
projects.reflection: Some preprocessing was performed before splitting, and model selection used test accuracy. These evaluation choices are important limitations and lessons for future experiments.
projects.cardOutcome: Prediction app published; Docker image built and run locally.

projects.title: Visora
projects.summary: A three-person coursework project combining object detection with spoken descriptions.
projects.motivation: Explore software that could help blind people identify objects in front of a camera. The original idea included assistive glasses.
projects.contribution: I handled text-to-speech and addressed overlapping speech through queue-based playback. The same team continued the project from an AI class into Deep Learning.
projects.approach: The software connects object labels to speech output. A single-pending-item queue replaces older pending speech so the output can keep up with the scene. Repository code includes pretrained SpeechT5 integration.
projects.outcome: I observed the final software working without the earlier crashes or overlapping voices. The glasses hardware was not built, and no user study was conducted.
projects.reflection: Real-time systems need coordination between inference and output; speech can become unusable if every result competes for playback.
projects.cardOutcome: Observed speech playback working without the earlier overlapping voices.

projects.title: Music Genre Classifier
projects.summary: Exploring the GTZAN dataset before training a music genre classifier.
projects.motivation: Connect my interest in music with practical audio-data exploration and machine learning.
projects.contribution: This is an individual project developed with AI guidance. Current work is focused on understanding and preparing the dataset.
projects.approach: Saved notebook work includes audio inspection, file-readability checks, duplicate detection, and grouped train/validation/test preparation.
projects.outcome: Audio exploration and data preparation are ongoing. Classifier training and evaluation are the next stages.
projects.reflection: Dataset quality and split design deserve attention before training begins.
projects.cardOutcome: Audio inspection and dataset preparation; model training is still ahead.

projects.title: Spoken-Command Research
projects.summary: Studying how quantization and calibration data affect spoken-command recognition under previously unseen noise.
projects.motivation: Understand how model compression and calibration choices interact with noisy audio conditions.
projects.contribution: I handle experiments; my teammate handles writing. This is ongoing coursework research.
projects.approach: The research workflow compares FP32, static post-training quantization, and quantization-aware training for DS-CNN keyword spotting, using clean/noisy/mixed development conditions and unseen-noise evaluation.
projects.outcome: Experiments and pipeline development are ongoing. I’m preparing the paper for submission to a conference as part of the Research Methodology course.
projects.reflection: The project is giving me experience with controlled comparisons, reproducibility, and experimental checks.
projects.cardOutcome: Quantization experiments ongoing; conference submission planned.

projects.title: Loan Approval MLOps
projects.summary: A separate individual coursework assignment comparing loan-approval classifiers and packaging a prediction application.
projects.motivation: Practise the steps between a tabular dataset, model comparison, and application deployment.
projects.contribution: I designed the workflow, ran notebooks, reviewed results, published the app, and ran Docker, with AI implementation and debugging assistance.
projects.approach: The assignment used 2,000 records and compared Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost. The prediction workflow uses income, credit score, loan amount, and years employed.
projects.outcome: Completed coursework with saved model artifacts, an application, and documented deployment.
projects.reflection: Scaling before the split and selecting by test accuracy limit the evaluation; future workflows should separate fitting and selection more carefully.
projects.cardOutcome: Coursework app and model artifacts completed, with documented deployment.

projects.title: GEMASTIK 2026 Data Mining: Paddy-Drying Prediction
projects.summary: A team project exploring weather-based paddy-drying prediction with physics simulation and machine learning.
projects.motivation: Explore how weather information could support decisions around drying harvested paddy.
projects.contribution: I developed the idea and wrote the paper in a three-person competition team.
projects.approach: The team paper combines weather windows and physics-generated drying labels with machine-learning comparisons. Reported predictions concern simulated targets, rather than validated field measurements.
projects.outcome: Our three-person team passed BINUS internal selection and represented BINUS at GEMASTIK 2026 with this paddy-drying prediction project.
projects.reflection: The concept needs real drying measurements before field performance or agricultural impact could be established.
projects.cardOutcome: Passed internal selection and represented BINUS in a three-person team.

projects.title: Ubuntu Homelab
projects.short: A second life for an older laptop.
projects.summary: An Ubuntu host for personal services, remote access, and AI experiments.
projects.motivation: Have a practical place to explore self-hosting and keep personal services running.
projects.contribution: I operate and experiment with the setup, using guidance when needed for configuration and troubleshooting.
projects.approach: Ubuntu Server CLI hosts Mordred’s backend, Minecraft, and an image-generation interface connected to the ComfyUI API, with remote access through Tailscale.
projects.outcome: A working environment for learning about services and deployment. Hardware details are listed on the About page.
projects.reflection: Running these services gives me practice with configuration, storage, and troubleshooting.
projects.cardOutcome: Hosts personal services with remote access through Tailscale.
